title: Declarative capacity target controller with failsafe fencing
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Goal: Implement a declarative controller that accepts high-level throughput/latency targets and produces safe scaling decisions for Dedicated fleets. The controller should centralize target-to-action translation so product teams can specify SLOs (e.g., 99th-tail latency < 120ms, sustained throughput 12k req/s) while the runtime enforces safety fences (min/max replicas, surge caps, cooldown) and cost-aware fallbacks.

Scope:
- Input model: declarative SLO object (throughput target, latency quantiles, optional cost cap, tenant priority).
- Output: discrete scale actions (add/remove N instances, change instance class or model-variant routing) with annotated safety rationale.
- Algorithms: hybrid approach combining demand forecast + conservative controller (bounded derivative/step) with a PID-inspired smoothing layer and emergency circuit-breaker for overload.
- Safety: explicit limits (min_replicas, max_replicas), surge_rate ceilings, per-tenant burst credits, cooldown windows, and rollback triggers when downstream latency or error rate worsens.
- Observability: expose decision rationale, estimated headroom, anticipated cost delta, and tie actions to traceable audit entries and PR IDs.

Why different from existing autoscalers: existing components focus on single-signal scaling (throughput or latency) or aggressive ML-driven forecasts. This ticket defines a declarative contract for SLOs and a safety-first decision engine that blends forecasts with conservative actuators so production apps get predictable behavior and clear governance for Dedicated customers.
acceptance_criteria: Controller accepts declarative SLO JSON and returns scale plan with actions and safety tags in staging cluster
Scale actions obey configured min/max and surge limits in 1000 randomized sim runs
System prevents more-than-configured replica churn per cooldown window in canary run
Metrics emitted for decision rationale (headroom_estimate, predicted_rps, cost_delta) visible in console dashboard
Fail-open/fail-closed behavior documented and validated: on metric telemetry loss, controller uses conservative hold policy and emits alert
notes: Prototype algorithm evaluated against production traces (see /drive/autoscale/trace-replay/experiment-2026-02-10) showing 18% lower peak overprovision vs simple stepper with equivalent tail latency
Security: RBAC for who can change SLOs + audit logs required for enterprise tenants
Pricing: controller will surface estimated cost impact; billing integration ticket in scope for later cycle
